Arguments passed to mypy: ` --ignore-missing-imports --linecoverage-report build --show-traceback`

Removing the line coverage flag bypasses the error.
@euresti You might be interested in this, it _may_ be related to attrs plugin (I mean the last proposed repro for the crash).
Based on the repro Guido posted I don't think it's the attrs plugin only.  I wonder if it's caused by #4544

Ok never mind.  I see a problem but I'm not sure what to do about it.

All the methods I add for attrs are given the same line number as the class they are created in.
i.e. `func.line = self.info.line`  But this means that the line coverage report thinks there's a method that starts at that line.  And it goes looking for it and doesn't find it and hits the assertion.

However to add insult to injury, when you add a decorator to a class, the `TypeInfo.line` seems to return the line number of the first decorator not the line number of the "class ...."  which doesn't help or hurt here.

I also looked at NamedTuple to see why that wasn't hitting this problem and I found the reason why we're going into this code path to begin with.  It's this at the bottom of add_method:
```
        # Add the created methods to the body so that they can get further semantic analysis.
        # e.g. Forward Reference Resolution.
        self.info.defn.defs.body.append(func)
```

So what do you suggest?  I could add something to the FuncDef that says that this is a manufactured method or something like that.  Or I could figure out some other way to do the further semantic analysis needed.

@euresti That's a good question. Some way to distinguish generated methods might be the way to go.

In the mean time, I've put up a fix that makes coverage reports more resilient to dodgy line numbers.

issue.title: Fix crashes in coverage reports
issue.body:
There are two parts to this:
 1. Look harder for the start of a function, since decorators can make
    it tricky to find.
 2. Be more defensive about handling dodgy line number info.
    Our line numbers aren't reliable enough to be crashing the
    reporter over. This fixes a crash related to attrs.

Fixes #4563
